key_insight: GLOBE uses the geometry of reasoning trajectories to stop chain-of-thought generation early, reducing computation while maintaining performance comparable to full reasoning.
engineering_relevance: This online, training-free approach could lower inference costs and latency in mathematical reasoning, tool-calling, and agent-memory workloads.
method: Embed each completed reasoning segment as a point on a unit sphere.
Generate short trial answers in a separate branch and stop the main stream when a trial passes a confidence threshold.
If reasoning continues, stop when the semantic trajectory repeatedly reverses direction with little net progress.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks and two models, GLOBE reduced output tokens by 49.7% and active end-to-end wall time by 51.0%, achieving a five-task average score of 80.58%, comparable to Full CoT.
watch_item: Confidence thresholds and trajectory stopping criteria may need validation on new models and tasks to avoid premature exits.
paper_title: GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories
